items.problem: Migrated ApplyChanges_Click dropped 'configuration.Ssid = SsidTextBox.Text;' (D1) — a real behavioral fidelity defect that took requirement #1 from pass to partial (score 75).
items.evidence: session-log.txt L2563 edit: old_str included '...GetCurrentAccessPointConfiguration();\n\n    configuration.Ssid = SsidTextBox.Text;', new_str reproduced only '...GetCurrentAccessPointConfiguration();' — the assignment was deleted while the intended change was merely adding a '!' null-forgiving operator to m_tetheringManager. discrepancies.json d1-apply-drops-ssid; migration-score.json feature 'Configure Mobile Hotspot' verdict partial.
items.covered_at: SKILL.md > Critical Rules > Fidelity (highest priority), bullet at line 181 ('edit that copy in place, changing only the lines an API/namespace transform requires' and 'the validator's verbatim-text check ... inspects XAML only, so a wholesale .cs rewrite is unguarded').
items.why_missed: grey-zone / under-emphasized — the Fidelity rule targets *wholesale* .cs overwrites (Set-Content/here-strings) and *visible text*, but does not call out the subtler and more common failure: a targeted string-replace whose old_str is widened to include an adjacent statement that the new_str then silently drops. The dev-agent was doing exactly the endorsed 'edit in place' path, so it did not read this as a warning that applied to it.
items.proposed_improvement: Add one Fidelity bullet on surgical-edit hygiene: every line in an edit's match window except the single line being transformed must be reproduced verbatim in the replacement; the classic silent defect is a one-token change (e.g. adding '!') whose old_str swept in a following statement dropped from new_str; after any in-place .cs edit, re-read the replaced block and confirm the only diff is the intended transform (compiler + XAML-only verbatim check will not catch a dropped statement).
items.generalizes: UWP→WinUI migration is overwhelmingly done via many targeted string-replace edits (namespace rewrites, null-forgiving operators, API swaps). Collateral deletion of an adjacent statement is a model-agnostic edit hazard that recurs on any code-behind that sets several properties before an async call (ConfigureAsync/SaveAsync/etc.), independent of this scenario's APIs.

items.problem: On the gated machine the WinUI app shows the generic 'This sample could not initialize on this machine. <ex>' where the UWP shows the specific 'This app is not configured to access Wi-Fi devices on this machine.' (D2, minor).
items.evidence: session-log.txt L1640 edit wraps OnNavigatedTo init in try/catch whose catch does NotifyUser('This sample could not initialize on this machine. {ex.Message}'); the source Helpers path still contains the specific capability message. discrepancies.json d2-gated-status-text.
items.covered_at: SKILL.md > Critical Rules > Defensive UI for init-heavy and device-dependent pages, the 'Rule:' paragraph (lines 224-227) which prescribes the generic 'This sample could not initialize on this machine.' fallback.
items.why_missed: under-emphasized — the Defensive-UI rule tells the agent to add the generic fallback but does not say to preserve a source-specific failure message when the source already surfaces one, so a blanket catch masks the precise message.
items.proposed_improvement: Add a short clause to the Defensive-UI Rule: if the source's own init/helper path already surfaces a specific user-facing message on the failure it expects (e.g. a capability-gated NotifyUser that returns gracefully), let that path run and catch only genuinely unexpected exceptions; use the generic fallback text only when the source had none.
items.generalizes: SDK samples and device-dependent apps frequently carry precise capability/error messages on their degradation paths; a reflexive blanket try/catch that always emits the generic text erodes text parity across any such migration, not just this one.
